narrative.overview:
The site looks like a well-run staff board: organised rows, calm colours, and one teal marker that points at what matters. Deep Harbour Navy frames every page top and bottom (nav bar and footer), cool Harbour Mist bands separate sections, and white cards and tables carry the content. Teal is the only accent, and it marks the things a visitor should act on or notice: buttons, active links, plan badges, ticks.

The feel is friendly and dependable. Corners are soft, motion is a gentle lift, and nothing shouts. It is aimed at small-business owners, not developers, so the system leans on familiar patterns (sticky nav, card grid, comparison table, three pricing cards) and keeps them tidy rather than inventing new ones. The tokens live once, in `assets/site.css`, shared by the landing page, docs and blog.
keyCharacteristics: Navy frame, mist bands, white content surfaces, one teal accent.
System font stack throughout; weight (700–800) does the hierarchy work, not a display face.
Soft 8–14px corners; pills for badges; circles for step numbers.
Flat at rest; a soft teal glow and a 1–2px lift appear only on hover.
Tables are a first-class component: navy header, mist zebra rows, green ticks and faded red crosses.

rules.name: The One Marker Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only accent colour. Plan buttons named navy, amber and purple in the CSS all render teal; keep it that way. A second accent would turn the board into noise.

rules.name: The Navy Frame Rule
rules.body: Every page opens with the navy nav bar and closes with the navy footer. Navy is also the colour of headings, so content always reads as part of the same frame.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Bright Sea Glass Teal never carries text and never sits behind white text; both fail contrast. Teal text uses Teal Ink on light surfaces and Teal Light on navy; teal fills carry navy text.

rules.name: The Tint, Don't Paint Rule
rules.body: Teal and status colours appear on large areas only as faint tints (6–18% alpha backgrounds, 25–35% alpha borders), as in callouts, plan badges and the hero badge. Solid teal is reserved for small action surfaces.

rules.name: The Weight Does the Work Rule
rules.body: Never add a second typeface for emphasis. Step up the weight (700 → 800) or the size; colour headings navy.

rules.name: The Lift on Touch Rule
rules.body: Surfaces only rise in response to the pointer: buttons move up 1px, cards up 2px with the teal glow. The featured pricing card is the single exception that glows at rest.

dos: Do use Sea Glass Teal for every action and highlight, and Sea Glass Teal Deep for its hover.
Do alternate white and Harbour Mist sections, separated by 1px Tide Line borders.
Do colour headings and `strong` text Deep Harbour Navy and running copy Slate Muted.
Do keep comparison data in the navy-header table with ✓ / ✗ and `cell-note` caveats.
Do link `assets/site.css` and `assets/site.js` from every new page instead of redefining tokens; landing, docs and blog all use the same values.
Do keep hover motion small: 1px lift for buttons, 2px plus teal glow for cards, and drop the lift under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do put navy text on teal fills, Teal Ink for teal text on light surfaces, and Teal Light for teal text on navy.
Do rely on `assets/site.css` for the focus ring, selection colour, skip link, mobile nav and reduced motion; don't re-declare them per page.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent colour; tier buttons stay teal regardless of their class names.
Don't add a display or web font; the system stack is part of the WordPress-native feel.
Don't use grey drop shadows on content surfaces; content shadows are teal-tinted and appear on hover only.
Don't paint large areas solid teal; use tints (6–18% alpha) for backgrounds and borders.
Don't use sharp 0px corners on cards or buttons.
Don't put white text on any teal, or use bright Sea Glass Teal as a text colour.
Don't hide navigation on small screens without a menu button to reach it.
